text:
maria-cs: 🚨 Support escalation from ACME (tenant acme-prod). Multiple 5xx/timeouts from hosted inference during a mid-day burst, started ~15:22 UTC. Customer reports ~30% of requests returning 502/504, latency jumps to 8-12s. Request IDs: req=0b3f,0b40,0b41. Attaching sample trace and gateway logs.

maria-cs: logs snippet:
```
proxy.gateway: upstream timeout waiting for response (tenant=acme-prod) req=req=0b3f path=/v1/generate code=504
runtime: failed to allocate nvmem for model init, retrying
```

maria-cs: CS asks for root cause and ETA. Marking P1 for now. @devon-oncall can you triage? :eyes:

devon-oncall: on it. I'm seeing burst at 15:21-15:26 with queued requests spike. Gateway shows scaleup attempts but pods remain Pending for ~20-40s. KEDA scaledobject metrics show scaledThreshold hit but no ready pods.

devon-oncall: quick checks: `kubectl get pods -n tenant-acme` shows pods stuck in ContainerCreating, waiting for mount and GPU scheduling. Node logs show image pull + plugin init delays. Also noticed a recent node-affinity change pushed yesterday evening that routes acme workloads to the gpu-heavy pool with lower spare capacity.

kai-eng-sre: +1 to node-affinity suspicion. Also the readiness/liveness timings for the model init container are aggressive. We have `readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds=5` and `periodSeconds=10` on the model sidecar — for big models that can cause probe flapping and KEDA perceiving them as unready. Suggest increasing initialDelay and adding a warmupProbe.

ashley-engruntime: adding runtime data: model init for gpt-xx on those nodes takes ~18-22s when cold (checkpoint load + quant kernel warmup). If pods land on nodes under memory pressure that can stretch to 35s. So 5s probe is definitely too short.

ron-support: Customer timeline: errors started when traffic doubled during scheduled marketing blast. They were routed to hosted inference region us-west-2. They asked why fallback to smaller model didn't happen.

devon-oncall: fallback policy didn't trigger because we route by tenant-policy and fallback variants were in a different AZ with capacity constraints. Also observed that KEDA pollingInterval is 30s (default) which delays scale down/up reactions — combined with HPA minReplicas=0 leads to cold starts.

devon-oncall: repro steps I ran:
1) replayed a 2x QPS burst against /v1/generate for tenant acme-prod with seq_len=1024
2) monitored scaledobject metrics and k8s events
3) observed pods Created -> ContainerCreating ~20-40s -> Running
4) gateway started returning 502/504 while pod readiness pending

kai-eng-sre: mitigation suggestions:
- bump readinessProbe.initialDelaySeconds to 30 and timeoutSeconds to 60 for model init container
- set KEDA `pollingInterval` to 5s for this scaledobject and set `cooldownPeriod` to 60s
- set minReplicaCount to 1 for high-QPS tenants (acme-prod)
- add a startup annotation `redwood.io/warmup=true` so runtime triggers KV-prefetch before readiness

ashley-engruntime: operational quick patch: we can push an autoscale override for acme-prod to minReplicas=1 and temporarily enable region fallback routing for 10m to kube-pool-b (has spare GPUs). I'll prepare a rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: autoscale-override/acme-prod -> minReplicas=1 by ashley-engruntime. CI checks ok. ETA deploy in ~2m.

billing-bot: note: routing to fallback region may change egress costs for tenant; flagged to billing for awareness (ticket #BILL-8421).

maria-cs: I told customer we'll apply a temporary override and follow up with config changes so this doesn't recur. CS asked for a short postmortem and permanent remediations.

devon-oncall: after override applied: observed immediate reduction in 5xxs within 90s and queue drained. We'll schedule a follow-up to roll config changes into the tenant profile: readinessProbe bump, KEDA polling tweak, minReplicas policy, and node-affinity rollback.

kai-eng-sre: action items:
- (kai) open infra PR to revert affinity rule that pushed acme to low-spare pool (PR draft)
- (ashley) temp override + enable fallback routing (done)
- (devon) create an incident postmortem and include repro steps/metrics + dashboard links
- (maria) CS follow-up message + customer timeline

ron-support: customer ok with temporary fix; requested ETA for permanent fix. I'll keep them updated.

maria-cs: assigning owners and closing slack loop; moving to incident tracker INS-4987 for full postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
